data.cultural_impact: Srutkirt carries an elegant and profound meaning rooted in the rich heritage of Indian culture. In ancient India, learning was revered upon as a sacred duty, nurtured to bring wisdom, transform lives and contribute to society. The name Srutkirt instills a sense of respect for education and knowledge, reminding us of the profound value placed on learning in Indian culture. More broadly, the name represents an individual who has gained renown for their wisdom and knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Srutkirt holds great spiritual significance as it pertains to two crucial aspects of individuals' lives: knowledge and karma. In Hinduism, knowledge is spoken of as the purest form of devotion and path to the ultimate truth. The spiritual practice of gaining knowledge is seen as a means to self-realization and a means to keep at bay the negative influences of ignorance. Furthermore, the name Srutkirt suggests that this individual's fame, or kirt, arises from their spiritual growth and pursuit of wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Srutkirti was a famous Hindu philosopher from the Nalanda University in Magadha, India, during the Pala Empire (circa 750-1200 CE). He is known for his contributions to the field of Nyaya-Vaisheshika philosophy, particularly his work 'The Catuhsutras'.

Another reference to Srutkirti can be found in the Prabodhacandrodaya, a 16th century Bengali language devotional text. In this text, Srutkirti is described as a great scholar who was initiated into the Rasik tradition of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (circa 15th-16th century CE).
